title: FROZEN METHODOLOGY 08 - Adversarial / Edge-case Case Set, Early Error Detection Stage Scoring, and Debuggability Protocol
status: FROZEN. Authored before any language was measured. No field in this document may be altered after measurement of any language has begun (spec 25.4, 32). A defect discovered later is recorded as a published erratum in the results, never as a silent edit here.
intended_reader: An operator who has never seen the conversation that produced this file. Every decision in this document is mechanical: a build command, a run command, a string comparison, a regular expression, or a cited normative clause.

fairness_statement.derivation: Every case in this file was derived exclusively from the 26 hazards enumerated verbatim in spec section 17, from the stage ladder in spec sections 18 and 25.1.F, and from general programming-language theory. No Quidra documentation, source, grammar, example, operator table, type list or feature list was consulted while authoring the case set.
fairness_statement.quidra_is_the_subject_not_the_designer: Quidra is the language under evaluation. The purpose of this case set is NOT to make Quidra score well. Quidra is expected to score badly on any case where it behaves badly, and each of the other nine languages is free to score 100 on any case Quidra fails.
fairness_statement.capabilities_quidra_may_lack_are_retaine: No hazard was removed, softened, or reworded because Quidra may lack the construct required to express it. Cases requiring unsigned fixed-width integers, uninitialized storage, unchecked casts, raw pointers, explicit immutability, or null/absent references are retained in full for all ten languages.
fairness_statement.languages_may_beat_quidra: No case is constructed so that a particular language must win. Every case rewards the same thing in every language: refusing, diagnosing, or preventing the hazardous operation as early as possible; and every case punishes the same thing in every language: completing normally with a wrong value that looks valid.
fairness_statement.symmetry_of_construction: Each case specifies one language-neutral hazardous situation and one fixed sequence of operations. The same sequence is implemented in all ten languages. No language receives an extra guard, an extra check, a different algorithm, a different data structure, a different build flag, or a different observation format.
fairness_statement.known_asymmetries_are_disclosed_not_corr: Several frozen recipes disable checks that a different flag would enable (for example rustc -O disables debug_assertions, so integer overflow wraps rather than panicking; zig -OReleaseFast disables safety checks; clang++ -O2 runs no sanitizer). These are properties of the frozen recipes in environment/environment.json, which were fixed before this document. They are NOT corrected here for any language. They are instead measured, published, and additionally re-observed in the non-scoring secondary configuration of section 'secondary_non_scoring_configurations' so that no inconvenient fact is hidden (spec 32).
fairness_statement.no_post_hoc_redesign: Cases, reference observations, plausibility predicates, diagnostic lexicons, stage scores, subset memberships and weights in this file must not be changed in response to observed results (spec 25.4, 32).

fixed_column_order_note: Quidra, Python, C++, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift, Zig. This order is used in every table produced under this methodology, without exception.

toolchain_binding.rule: Adversarial programs are built and run with exactly those recipes and no other flag, package, sanitizer, tsconfig.json, build file, or code generator. Where a recipe has a build step, the build step is the compile stage referred to by the decision procedure; where it has none (Python), the language has no compile stage and can never reach the 'Compile-time Detection' rung of the ladder. That is a real, measured property of the language as configured, not a penalty applied by this methodology.
toolchain_binding.typescript_note: No tsconfig.json may exist in the build directory. The frozen recipe is the bare `tsc FILE.ts` command, so tsc's CLI defaults apply (in particular `strict` and `strictNullChecks` are off unless tsc's own default for version 7.0.2 turns them on). Whatever tsc 7.0.2 does by default with no configuration file is what is measured. The operator records tsc's effective options once, by running `tsc --showConfig` in an empty directory, and stores the output as evidence.
toolchain_binding.quidra_mode_rule: Quidra's SCORED observation for every case is taken from native compiled mode (`quidra build` then `./BIN`), because every other language is likewise scored in exactly one frozen configuration. Interpreter mode (`quidra run FILE.qui`) is executed for every case as well and recorded in full as a separate, published, NON-SCORING row. Where native and interpreter mode disagree on the recorded stage for a case, the divergence must be published in a dedicated 'Quidra native vs interpreter adversarial divergence' table in the Adversarial / Safety results. This rule is fixed here, before any result is examined, as spec section 11 requires.
toolchain_binding.host: Apple M2, 8 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, macOS 26.4.1 arm64

execution_environment.working_directory: One fresh, empty directory per (case, language, configuration) triple, created by the harness.

environment_variables.note: PYTHONUTF8, PYTHONIOENCODING, RUST_BACKTRACE, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, NODE_OPTIONS and GOFLAGS must be UNSET. The harness must clear them explicitly. No other variable may be set to influence behaviour.

execution_environment.stdin: Supplied from the case's frozen input file, or /dev/null when the case declares no input.
execution_environment.stdout_stderr: Captured to separate files. They are never merged.
execution_environment.repetitions_rule: Each (case, language) is built once and run 5 times in the primary configuration. All 5 runs are preserved. Byte-identity of the OBS line across all 5 runs is a required input to the Undefined Behavior test (D7a). Timing is not a scored quantity in this methodology.
execution_environment.resource_limits: No ulimit, cgroup, or memory limit is imposed. The huge-allocation case requests a byte count larger than the 64-bit address space so that it fails immediately rather than driving the host into swap.
execution_environment.concurrency: Cases are run one at a time. No other benchmark workload may run concurrently.

mandatory_program_skeleton.purpose: Makes 'did execution begin?', 'did the program reach its observation point?' and 'what did it observe?' mechanically decidable in all ten languages with no language-specific interpretation.
steps: S1. Write the exact ASCII line `ADV-START` followed by U+000A to standard output, and flush standard output immediately.

S2. If the case declares inputs, read them from standard input, one token per line, in the declared order, using the language's ordinary line-reading facility. Each token is converted with the conversion the case names (see each case's `inputs`). This step is the opacity barrier; see `opacity_barrier`.
S3. Perform the case's hazardous operation, exactly and only as the case's `construction` specifies.
S4. Write the exact ASCII text `OBS=` followed by the case's observation payload and U+000A to standard output, and flush standard output immediately.
S5. Write the exact ASCII line `ADV-END` followed by U+000A to standard output, flush, and terminate with exit status 0.
prohibitions: P1. The program contains no exception handler, error recovery, signal handler, panic hook, `catch`, `except`, `recover`, `rescue`, `defer`-based recovery, `try`-block, `Result`/`Option` match, guard clause, range check, null check, validation, clamping, saturation, or any other construct whose purpose is to inspect or survive the hazard. The single exception is a construct the language forces on the author in order to compile at all, which must then be the shortest such construct available (see A3).
P2. No logging, timing, tracing, assertion, unit-test framework, or diagnostic printing beyond S1, S4 and S5.

P3. No compiler pragma, attribute, suppression, `#[allow]`, `@SuppressWarnings`, `// @ts-ignore`, `unchecked`, `-W` flag, or `unsafe`/`@setRuntimeSafety` block, unless the case's `construction` explicitly requires it for all languages that have such a construct.
P4. No third-party package. Only the language's own standard library, as shipped with the frozen toolchain.
P5. No output formatting that differs from the case's `observation_spec`. The OBS payload is compared as bytes.

authoring_rules.A1_equivalence: The ten implementations of a case must perform the same operations on the same values in the same order. An implementation that performs a different computation, uses a different data structure, or reaches the hazard by a different route is invalid and must be rewritten before any result is recorded.
authoring_rules.A2_idiomatic_minimality: Each implementation is the shortest ordinary program that performs the case's construction under the skeleton. It is written the way a competent, non-defensive author of that language would write it when not thinking about the hazard.
authoring_rules.A3_shortest_direct_use_rule: Where an operation in a language returns its result alongside a failure channel (an error value, an optional, a result type, a status flag, a second return value), the program USES THE RESULT DIRECTLY, in the shortest form that language provides for doing so, and does not inspect the failure channel. Examples of what this rule selects, stated so that it cannot be argued about later: Rust `.unwrap()`; Go `v, _ := f()`; Java the plain call whose failure is an unchecked exception; C++ the plain call; Swift `try!` or the non-optional initializer; Kotlin the non-null / non-Result form; TypeScript the plain call; Python the plain call. This rule is language-neutral in statement and its consequences differ between languages precisely because the languages differ. Those differing consequences ARE the measurement. They must not be equalised.
authoring_rules.A4_default_unqualified_form_rule: Where a language offers both a checked and an unchecked form of the same operation (conversion, cast, indexing, division, member access), the program uses the DEFAULT, UNQUALIFIED form: the form a reader writes when expressing no additional intent. It does not use a form whose name or syntax announces that the author was thinking about the hazard (`checked_*`, `try_into`, `truncatingIfNeeded`, `@truncate`, `wrapping_*`, `saturating_*`, `as?`, `get()` returning an optional, `at()` with bounds checking). Where the language offers only one form, that form is used.
authoring_rules.A5_fixed_identifiers: Identifier names are irrelevant to every measurement in this document and are not constrained.
authoring_rules.A6_compilability_precondition: Before any result is recorded, the operator must confirm that each implementation is the program the case describes, by reading it against the case's `construction` line by line. A mismatch is an authoring defect to be fixed before measurement, not a result.
authoring_rules.A7_no_substitution: A case may not be replaced, dropped, softened, or split after measurement begins. A case that cannot be run for a host or toolchain reason is marked N/A under `na_policy`, with the reason recorded.

opacity_barrier.why: Whether a hazard is visible to the compiler as a constant is a real difference between languages, but it is also an accident of how a test program is written. Two variants are therefore specified for every case whose hazardous value is a value at all, so that the constant-visible and runtime-only situations are both measured for all ten languages, and neither is confused with the other.

variants.C: STATIC VARIANT. The hazardous value appears in the source as a manifest constant expression, written plainly, with no obfuscation and no attempt to hide it from the compiler.
variants.R: DYNAMIC VARIANT. The hazardous value is obtained at run time by reading one line from standard input and converting it with the language's ordinary string-to-number (or string-to-boolean, or string) conversion, so that no compiler and no static checker can know it. The line's text is supplied by the harness from the case's frozen input file.

opacity_barrier.R_variant_parsing_rule: In the R variant, the input-parsing step itself must not be allowed to become the measured hazard. The input text for every case except ADV-25 is a well-formed token of the target type, and the program uses the shortest direct use rule (A3) to obtain it. If the parsing step itself fails or diagnoses in a language, that is recorded as an authoring defect and the case is re-authored for that language using a different ordinary parsing facility, BEFORE any result is recorded. ADV-25 is the one case where the malformed input IS the hazard.
opacity_barrier.scoring_unit: Each variant of each case is scored as its own row: the fixed adversarial case set is the set of case-variants, listed in `fixed_scored_case_variant_list`. Reporting them separately, rather than combining them, means an auditor can see both 'this language rejects the constant' and 'this language does not see it at run time' without either fact being averaged away.
opacity_barrier.cases_with_one_variant_only: Cases whose hazard is inherently a property of the source text (ADV-12 uninitialized storage, ADV-16 immutable mutation, ADV-18 missing return, ADV-21 parser nesting, ADV-22 malformed source, ADV-24 huge numeric literal) or of a file's bytes (ADV-23) have the single variant declared in the case's `variants` field. No case has a variant invented for it that its hazard does not admit.

type_binding_table.why: Phrases like 'the 64-bit signed integer type' must resolve to exactly one construct per language, decided before any measurement, or the result becomes an argument about which construct was fair.

default_arithmetic_type.meaning: The type an ordinary author gets when writing arithmetic on whole numbers without choosing a type.
default_arithmetic_type.Quidra: The type the Quidra documentation designates as the default integer type for ordinary arithmetic. The operator records the citation.
default_arithmetic_type.C++: long long (64-bit on this host); literals written plainly

fixed_width_i64.Quidra: Quidra's designated signed 64-bit two's-complement integer type; citation recorded. If Quidra has none, rule TM3 applies.
fixed_width_i64.Python: ctypes.c_int64 (Python's standard-library fixed-width integer TYPE; `struct` is a serialization facility and is deliberately not used for a type-conversion case)
fixed_width_i64.TypeScript: No fixed-width 64-bit signed integer type exists. Rule TM3 applies: `bigint` is used as TypeScript's designated exact 64-bit-capable integer type, and the absence of wrap-around is recorded as a property of the language, not as an exemption.

fixed_width_i32.Quidra: Quidra's designated signed 32-bit two's-complement integer type; citation recorded. If none, rule TM3 applies.
fixed_width_i32.TypeScript: An element of an Int32Array of length 1. This is the standard library's fixed-width signed 32-bit storage. Writing to the element performs the language's defined conversion.

fixed_width_u32.Quidra: Quidra's designated unsigned 32-bit integer type; citation recorded. If none, rule TM3 applies.
fixed_width_u32.Java: No unsigned integer type exists (JLS 4.2). Rule TM3 applies.
fixed_width_u32.TypeScript: An element of a Uint32Array of length 1.

float64.Quidra: Quidra's designated IEEE-754 binary64 type; citation recorded.

default_string_type.Quidra: Quidra's default string type; citation recorded.

default_ordered_sequence.meaning: The growable, integer-indexed sequence an ordinary author reaches for first.
default_ordered_sequence.Quidra: Quidra's default array/list type; citation recorded.
default_ordered_sequence.Zig: []i64 backed by std.ArrayList(i64) or a slice of an array, as the case requires

most_general_reference.meaning: The type through which a value of any declared type can be passed without its concrete type being known statically. Used only by ADV-13.
most_general_reference.Quidra: Quidra's most general reference/dynamic type; citation recorded. If none, rule TM3 applies.
most_general_reference.C++: void* obtained by taking the address of the value

null_or_absent_value.meaning: The value denoting 'no value'. Used only by ADV-17.
null_or_absent_value.Quidra: Quidra's null/none/absent value or the absent case of its optional type; citation recorded.

TM3_capability_absent_rule.statement: If a language genuinely lacks the construct a case requires, the operator records `construct_absent: true` together with a normative citation (document name, version, clause) proving the absence, and then applies exactly one of the following, deciding BEFORE running anything:
TM3_capability_absent_rule.TM3a: If the absence means the hazard cannot arise in that language at all - there is no value of the wrong width to narrow, no unsigned/signed confusion to have, no uninitialized location to read - then the recorded stage is `Prevented By Construction` (score 100) and the justification is published verbatim in the results. This is a real safety property of the language and is scored as such.
TM3_capability_absent_rule.TM3b: If the absence is only that the most direct spelling is missing, but the language's ordinary alternative reaches the same hazard, the alternative is used, named in the results, and the case proceeds normally.
TM3_capability_absent_rule.TM3c: A missing capability never becomes N/A (spec 26). N/A in this document is reserved for host or toolchain defects, defined under `na_policy`.

outcome_classes.ladder_has_eight_rungs: Spec section 18 and the fixed table in spec section 25.1.F use an eight-rung stage ladder that additionally contains `Static Checking Before Execution` between compile-time rejection and runtime safe detection. Every observation in this document therefore carries TWO recorded fields: `class` (one of the seven classes of spec 17) and `earliest_observable_stage` (one of the eight rungs of spec 25.1.F). Only `earliest_observable_stage` is scored.

class_to_stage_mapping.Compile-time Detection: stage `Compile-time Detection` when the frozen build recipe rejected the program; stage `Static Checking Before Execution` when the language has no build step (or the build passed) and the defect was reported before the first statement of the program executed.
class_to_stage_mapping.Test Failure: stage `Test Failure`. See `test_failure_reachability` - this rung is structurally unreachable in this case set and the reason is published.

prevented_by_construction.label: Prevented By Construction
prevented_by_construction.why_it_exists: Some languages make a hazard impossible rather than detecting it: Python's int does not overflow; Go has no uninitialized local; Java has no unsigned int type; a language whose stacks grow can complete a recursion another language cannot. In those cases the program runs to completion and produces the mathematically correct, specified result, so none of the seven failure classes applies. Recording such a language at any failure rung would be a fabricated defect, which spec 32 forbids.
prevented_by_construction.scoring: Scored identically to `Compile-time Detection`, i.e. 100. No score outside the fixed range of spec 25.1.F is introduced by it, and no fixed stage score in that table is altered by it.
prevented_by_construction.reporting_requirement: It must be printed with its own label in every table, never merged into `Compile-time Detection`, so that a reader can always distinguish 'the compiler rejected this' from 'this language cannot have this bug'.
prevented_by_construction.evidence_requirement: A `Prevented By Construction` record is only valid with (a) the program source showing that the hazardous operation was genuinely attempted, and (b) either an exact match against the case's `reference_observation`, or a TM3a capability-absence citation.

test_failure_reachability.status: structurally unreachable in this case set
test_failure_reachability.reason: The `Test Failure` rung means a defect caught by a test suite. The adversarial programs are single-purpose executables with no test harness, because the ten fixed languages do not have a uniformly available zero-dependency standard test runner on this host (Java would require JUnit, C++ has no standard runner, Kotlin's requires a framework). Adding a test framework for the subset of languages that have one, and not for the rest, would violate spec section 7 and spec section 32. The rung is therefore left empty here and remains in the recorded ladder, where it is exercised by the workload test suites of spec sections 13, 14 and 15.
test_failure_reachability.consequence_for_scoring: No case-variant in this set may be recorded at the `Test Failure` rung. If an operator believes a case produced one, the observation has been misclassified and must be re-run through the decision procedure.

fixed_stage_score_table.source: prompt.md section 25.1.F, reproduced verbatim. These numbers are fixed and must not be changed, reweighted, rescaled, or interpolated.

registered_addition.note: Pre-registered label described under outcome_classes.prevented_by_construction. Scored identically to Compile-time Detection; reported separately.

fixed_stage_score_table.early_error_detection_definition: Early Error Detection for a language is the arithmetic mean of that language's stage scores over the fixed adversarial case-variant set, using normalization family F of spec 25.1. Cases marked N/A under `na_policy` are excluded from both numerator and denominator, with the reason published (spec 26). All scores are clipped to [0,100] and reported to two decimal places; ranking uses unrounded values (spec 25.3).

adv_end_present (bool: stdout contains the exact line `ADV-END`)
obs_payload (the bytes following the first occurrence of `OBS=` on its line, excluding the terminating newline) or null
observation_record_inputs.signal_convention: When the harness runs a program through a shell, an exit status of 128+N denotes death by signal N. The harness must record the signal number separately and must not confuse a signal-derived status with an ordinary exit status. The harness executes the run recipe directly (no shell wrapper) and reads the wait status, so the signal is unambiguous.
observation_record_inputs.primary_run_selection: The classification uses run #1 as the representative run. Runs #2-#5 are used only by test D7a (byte-identity of the OBS line) and by test D5 consistency (if the 5 runs do not all reach the same rung, the case-language is recorded at the LOWEST-scoring rung observed, the divergence is flagged `run_to_run_rung_divergence: true`, and all five runs are published).

classification_procedure.form: A single ordered decision list. Evaluate D0, D1, D2, ... in order and STOP at the first rule that fires. The order is the temporal order of the build-and-run pipeline, which is why the rung it produces is by construction the EARLIEST stage at which the defect became observable (spec 17).

steps.condition: The case's TM3 capability-absence determination was made before running (see type_binding_table.TM3_capability_absent_rule) and TM3a applies.

substeps.condition: The build process died by a fatal signal, OR build_stderr/build_stdout matches `toolchain_failure_markers`.

steps.condition: The language has a build recipe, the build exits zero, but no runnable artifact was produced.
steps.note: This is a toolchain defect, not a language property, and must also be reported under Compiler / Interpreter Robustness.

steps.condition: The program was run; run_exit_status is non-zero (or the process died by signal) AND `ADV-START` is ABSENT from stdout.
steps.meaning: The defect was reported before the first statement of the program executed.

substeps.condition: The process died by a fatal-fault signal (SIGSEGV 11, SIGBUS 10, SIGILL 4, SIGFPE 8) or stderr matches `toolchain_failure_markers`.

substeps.note: This is the rung Python and any other build-less configuration reaches when a syntax or import-time error is raised before user code runs. It is 90, not 100, because the artifact was accepted for execution and the check happened inside the run step.

steps.condition: The run exceeded the frozen 60-second run timeout.
steps.reason: The program neither diagnosed nor completed. The defect is observable, but only by an external observer watching that the expected output never appears - which is exactly what output verification is. Record the captured partial stdout/stderr.

steps.condition: `ADV-START` is present AND the process terminated abnormally (non-zero exit status or death by signal).

substeps.condition: stdout or stderr matches at least one pattern in the CASE's `hazard_diagnostic_lexicon` (case-insensitive, matched against the concatenation of stdout and stderr).
substeps.note: A fatal signal does NOT by itself force Crash. A controlled abort (SIGABRT, SIGTRAP, SIGILL used as a trap instruction) accompanied by a runtime-emitted diagnostic that names the hazard is exactly what 'runtime safe detection' means: the runtime noticed the specific hazard, said so, and stopped before doing anything with the invalid value. Rust's `panicked at ... attempt to divide by zero` and Swift's `Fatal error: ... overflow` are Runtime Safe Detection even though both end in a signal.

substeps.condition: A runtime-emitted diagnostic exists and names some SPECIFIC hazard, but not one in this case's lexicon.
evidence_required: a one-line note on why it does not match the case lexicon
substeps.note: The runtime still stopped safely with a specific message, so the rung is unchanged; the mismatch must be published because it bears on Diagnostics and Debuggability.

substeps.condition: Otherwise - no diagnostic, or only a generic one with no hazard named.
substeps.note: This is the uncontrolled-fault case. It covers a bare `Segmentation fault: 11`, `Bus error: 10`, `Illegal instruction: 4`, `Abort trap: 6` with nothing written to stderr, an OS out-of-memory kill (SIGKILL 9), and a silent non-zero exit. The operative distinction from D5a is not which signal was raised but whether the language's runtime produced a message identifying what went wrong.

steps.crash_vs_runtime_safe_detection_summary: Runtime Safe Detection = the runtime diagnosed the specific hazard and stopped in a defined way. Crash = the process ended abnormally without the runtime saying what the hazard was. Both tests are performed on captured bytes, so neither depends on the auditor's judgement.

substeps.reason: The program reported success while failing to execute its own specified tail. Control flow was altered by the hazard (for example an optimizer exploiting an undefined construct) and the program still claimed to succeed.

substeps.condition: obs_payload equals the case's `reference_observation` byte for byte, AND the case's `reference_observation` is a concrete value (not the sentinel `DIAGNOSED_FAILURE`).
substeps.reason: The specified hazardous operation was performed and the language produced the mathematically correct, specified result. No defect exists to detect.

substeps.condition: Otherwise, evaluate the case's `plausible_domain_predicate` on obs_payload.

The predicate is FALSE - the printed observation is on its face not a legal result of the stated computation (it is `nan`, `inf`, `undefined`, `null`, `None`, empty, a sentinel, or outside the declared legal range).
substeps.reason: The defect reached the program's output but any consumer of that output would see immediately that it is not a valid answer. Nothing before the output caught it.

substeps.condition: The predicate is TRUE - the printed observation is an ordinary, apparently valid result of the stated computation, and it differs from the reference.
substeps.reason: This is the situation spec section 17 singles out: an invalid value was silently transformed into another apparently valid value and execution continued. D7 decides only whether this is recorded as Undefined Behavior or as Silent Bug.

steps.condition: Reached only from D6c-ii: the program completed normally and produced a wrong but apparently valid value.

substeps.condition: The 5 primary runs did not all produce a byte-identical OBS payload.

The language's secondary (checked / sanitizer / debug) configuration for this case, listed under `secondary_non_scoring_configurations`, either emits a report that names undefined, illegal or erroneous behaviour for this operation, or produces a DIFFERENT OBS payload from the primary configuration.
evidence_required: the sanitizer or runtime report verbatim
substeps.note: This is the ONLY point at which a non-scoring secondary configuration may affect a recorded stage, and it can only move a record between the two lowest rungs (5 and 0). It can never raise a record to a higher rung. The exception is declared here, before any measurement, so that it is applied identically to all ten languages.

substeps.condition: The language's own normative specification declares the constructed operation to have undefined, illegal, or unspecified-and-unbounded behaviour, cited in the observation record's `normative_citation` field as {document, version, clause}.

evidence_required: `normative_status`: either `defined` with a {document, version, clause} citation showing the language DEFINES this result, or `no_citation_found`
substeps.note: Default to Silent Bug rather than Undefined Behavior when nothing can be established. It is the more conservative claim - we observed a deterministic, wrong, plausible value - and the resulting 5-point difference is disclosed here rather than decided after seeing results.

steps.undefined_behavior_vs_silent_bug_summary: Both end with the program exiting 0 and a wrong, plausible value. They are separated by positive evidence, never by opinion. Undefined Behavior requires ONE of: (a) the observation is not reproducible across the 5 fixed runs; (b) a checked build or sanitizer reports undefined/illegal behaviour for this operation, or changes the answer; (c) a citable clause of the language's own specification says the operation is undefined. Silent Bug is everything else: a deterministic, specified-or-unspecified-but-stable wrong answer that the language happily produced and nothing complained about.
steps.ub_that_crashes_is_recorded_as_crash: A construct that is undefined behaviour in the language specification but which, under the frozen recipe, terminates the process abnormally is recorded at D5 as Runtime Safe Detection or Crash, NOT as Undefined Behavior. The ladder records the earliest stage at which the defect became OBSERVABLE, and an abnormal termination is more observable than a silent wrong value. The observation record must carry `ub_underlying: true` plus the citation, so that the fact is published and can be read off the raw table.

earliest_observable_stage_recording_rule.statement: The recorded `earliest_observable_stage` for a (case-variant, language) is the rung produced by the first rule that fires in the ordered list D0..D7, under the frozen PRIMARY configuration only.
earliest_observable_stage_recording_rule.why_this_is_the_earliest: The decision list walks the pipeline in strict temporal order: capability absence (before any tool runs) -> build -> artifact -> pre-execution validation -> execution start -> non-termination -> abnormal termination -> normal completion -> output comparison -> reproducibility and normative status. A rule can only fire once every earlier stage has been observed not to have caught the defect, so the rung that fires is by construction the earliest point at which the defect became observable.
earliest_observable_stage_recording_rule.audit_requirement: The observation record must include `stage_evidence`, an ordered list naming every rule that was evaluated and why it did not fire, ending with the rule that did. An auditor must be able to re-derive the rung from the captured build output, run outputs, exit statuses and signals alone.
earliest_observable_stage_recording_rule.secondary_configurations_never_set_the_s: Observations from the non-scoring secondary configurations never set `earliest_observable_stage`, with the single, pre-declared exception of D7b, which may only move a record between Undefined Behavior (5) and Silent Bug (0).
earliest_observable_stage_recording_rule.no_retroactive_promotion: If a later analysis shows that some tool COULD have caught the defect earlier under different flags, the recorded stage does not change. The recorded stage is what the frozen recipe actually produced. The alternative observation is published in the secondary table.

toolchain_failure_markers.purpose: Used by D1a, D2 and D3a to separate 'the compiler correctly rejected the program' from 'the compiler itself broke'.
